name: Spanish
review: built 2026-11-12 by Claude Fable 5.2 from the questionnaire answers, lexicon and visible paradigms, after two schedule reads and three blind fluency reads of the rows; 153 of 153 held-out rows pass, 19 of which the builder had seen by the orchestrator's error (tooling/experiments/renderer-process/es-acceptance.md); audited 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 against independently computed fire times over 1714 patterns, with repairs to Quartz days a named month lacks, minutes in several parts inside several hours, excepted minutes inside named hours, and years with a hole in a cadence; the sentence forms those repairs introduced have had no blind fluency read; repaired a second time 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 against the core's calendar facts (dateReach, open years, cadencePieces), the cross-language trap list and the Spanish usage notes: schedules that never fire or fire only in leap years say so, months that lack the day are not named, a union takes no exception, days of the month no longer wrap into the next month, the Monday-to-Friday forms name their days in place of «día laborable» and «día hábil» (the `workday` style field is gone), and year, minute, second and day sets in runs and cadences together are no longer lists; none of the sentence forms of either repair has had a blind fluency read; 2026-11-13: says when both day fields must match (a day field written from a star beside a restricted one, as in Vixie cron), in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from this rule book's seed and reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2; a blind Sonnet reader told these sentences from the union's 16 times of 16, and none has had a blind fluency read; amended 2026-11-14 by Claude Opus 5.5 on the maintainer's rulings: a cadence of hours that tiles the day from midnight is bare («cada 2 horas», no window, list or «todos los días»), one that tiles it from a later start names only its start («cada 2 horas desde la 1:00»), one that does not tile keeps both ends; a minute or second is said apart before such hours («en el minuto 30, cada 2 horas»); such hours filled by minutes are «cada minuto durante una hora cada 2 horas»; and no bracket shows a series of times any more (the bracket of stretches after hours filled by minutes is gone, with the windows it repeated); the rows were rewritten by hand from the amended rule book before the renderer changed, and nothing was blind-read; amended again 2026-11-14 by Claude Opus 5.5 on three further rulings: every second hour filled by a finer field is «en las horas pares» or «en las horas impares» (and hours named by when they begin, every second one, «de las horas impares de 5:00 a 23:00»); named seconds at minute 0 beside every hour or a tiling cadence are said from the hour («a los 15 segundos de la hora en punto, cada 2 horas»); and seconds filling a stretch of one clock time are a window to the second with their step («cada 10 segundos de 9:30:00 a 9:30:50»); the rows were rewritten by hand before the renderer changed, except two hard-case rows (`0-29 8-18/2`, `1 0 * * * *`) written while it changed, and nothing was blind-read; 2026-11-14, released stable on the full reading check: all 648 rows read by three Sonnet 5.5 readers briefed only in the language (4705 questions about moments, scored against an answer key that shares no code with the library), and each of the 1 questions most readers got wrong asked again alone of three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers: none was still misread by most readers of both (tooling/scripts/reading/recheck.mjs)
